cards.back: $T$ is linear if $T(x+y)=T(x)+T(y)$ and $T(cx)=cT(x)$ for all $x,y$ and scalars $c$.

cards.front: Matrix representation of a linear map
cards.back: For a linear map $T$, there is a matrix $A$ such that $T(x)=Ax$ once a basis is fixed.
If $P$ changes coordinates between bases, then $A_{\text{new}} = P^{-1}AP$.
Matrices $A$ and $B$ are similar if $B=P^{-1}AP$. Similar matrices represent the same linear map in different bases.
If $B=P^{-1}AP$, then $A$ and $B$ have the same determinant, trace, and eigenvalues.
